about: Vans Electroengineerings makes vacuum circuit breakers and vacuum interrupters used in traction power supply for Indian Railways electrification and metro systems. It manufactures at Salem, Tamil Nadu, holds RDSO and CORE vendor approvals, and sells mainly to railway EPC contractors. Revenue was Rs 22.84 crore in FY26.

objects.purpose: General corporate purposes (capped at 15% of gross proceeds or Rs 10 crore, whichever is lower)

promoters.background: Chairman Balakrishnan Srinivasan has over 35 years in electrical engineering; Abhishek Saraff 23 years and Pooja Bansal 20 years; Viraj Bansal about 6 years. Promoters sold small stakes at Rs 118 per share in Sept 2026.

concentration.note: Top 1 customer 42.66% and top 5 customers 65.74% of FY26 revenue (97.48% in FY24). About 93.3% of FY26 revenue came via railway EPC contractors/vendors and 6.7% directly from Railways (B2G 6.7% vs B2B 93.3% per this split; business table shows B2B 86.76%, B2G 13.24%).

litigation_note: Company has 1 tax proceeding filed by it and none against it. Promoters: 3 criminal cases filed by them (Rs 0.89 crore) and 1 tax proceeding against them (Rs 0.05 crore). KMP/senior management: Rs 0.29 crore claim against.
strengths: Niche focus on railway vacuum circuit breakers and interrupters with RDSO approval and CORE developmental/approved vendor status, which creates entry barriers.
Revenue grew from Rs 2.60 crore in FY24 to Rs 22.84 crore in FY26, with FY26 EBITDA margin of 31.63% and PAT margin of 23.61%.
Order book of about Rs 50.62 crore as of Sept 5, 2026, more than twice FY26 revenue.
Low debt: borrowings of Rs 2.55 crore against net worth of Rs 9.17 crore (debt/equity 0.28).
In-house design, assembly and testing at Salem, with tests done at CPRI and KERI and ISO 9001:2015 certification.
Installed capacity is only 16% to 43% utilised, leaving room to grow volumes without new plant.
Experienced promoters, including a Chairman with over 35 years in electrical engineering.
Plans to widen the range into earthing switches and single bottle circuit breakers.

risks.title: Heavy customer concentration
risks.detail: Top 1 customer was 42.66% and top 5 customers 65.74% of FY26 revenue, with no long-term contracts. Loss of a key buyer would hurt sharply.

risks.title: Dependence on Indian Railways
risks.detail: Business depends on railway electrification spending and policy; about 93.3% of FY26 revenue came through railway EPC contractors and vendors, 6.7% directly from Railways.

risks.title: Receivables jumped, cash flow negative
risks.detail: Trade receivables rose to Rs 13.14 crore, about 58% of FY26 revenue, and operating cash flow was negative Rs 3.07 crore despite Rs 5.39 crore profit.

risks.title: Very short operating history
risks.detail: Incorporated in February 2022. FY24 profit was only Rs 0.02 crore, so the sharp profit growth rests on two years of results.

risks.title: Rising working capital need and seasonality
risks.detail: Working capital need is Rs 11.15 crore in FY26 and projected at Rs 27.71 crore in FY27. Revenue is skewed, with 75.33% earned in the second half of FY26.

risks.title: IPO funds only working capital
risks.detail: Rs 25 crore of proceeds goes to working capital with no capacity expansion; projections assume receivable days of 94 to 99 and inventory growth from Rs 2.20 crore to Rs 11.08 crore.

risks.title: Related party dealings and director loans
risks.detail: Company has borrowed from directors (Nitin Jain, Abhishek Saraff) and transacts with director-linked firms such as Sumo Pullman (commission paid), Sriwin Electric and Global Switchgear.

risks.title: Leased premises and small scale
risks.detail: Salem factory and registered office run on rent agreements, some for 11 months only. Plant is a single site in Tamil Nadu; FY26 revenue is just Rs 22.84 crore.

notes: RHP for BSE SME issue; price band, issue price, P/E and total issue size blank.
